text: program takes raw text individual names input returns data frame name parsed component parts: SALUTATION FIRST_NAME MIDDLE_NAME LAST_NAME SUFFIX STATUS GENDER GENDER_CONFIDENCE matching done probabilistically based upon frequencies name appearing first name last name US birth certificates. Set sanitize = TRUE input still contains punctuation, titles, clutter: parse_names() function utilizes parallelization speed large jobs.

title: All variants in a first name's family — first_name_variants
text: x first name (single string; case ignored). gender "U" (default), "M" "F". Gender can change canonical form nickname (PAT) family. related Logical; include related names merged (in_canonical = FALSE). Defaults TRUE. min_freq Drop names fewer national Part VII records (misspellings rare). Defaults 0 (keep ). min_share Share nickname evidence top formal name needs. Defaults 0.6. min_nick_rate Minimum ratio people carrying name nickname (people name formal form) national records name, name resolved. Defaults 0.002. spelling spelling pairs define spelling roots: "lexicon" (reviewed spelling pairs), "misspelling" (rare forms common names), "sound_alike" (unreviewed sound-alike pairs). Defaults c("lexicon", "misspelling").

title: All variants in a first name's family — first_name_variants

text: dataset intended use name-parsing, record linkage, entity resolution applications, providing consistent reference recognizing expanding abbreviated titles personal organizational names. type field groups abbreviation broad semantic categories : Personal Title: honorifics like "Mr", "Ms", "Dr". Academic Degree: academic professional degrees (e.g., "PhD", "MD", "MBA"). Religious Title: ecclesiastical clerical designations (e.g., "Rev", "Fr", "Sister"). Civic / Political Title: governmental judicial titles (e.g., "Senator", "Judge", "Honorable"). Military Rank / Affiliation: formal ranks affiliations (e.g., "Lt", "Col", "USAF"). Professional Credential: licensed certified professional credentials (e.g., "CPA", "PE", "RN"). Organizational Role: internal titles positions (e.g., "CEO", "VP", "Ex Officio"). Religious Order: post-nominals religious congregations (e.g., "SJ", "OSB", "RSM"). Fraternal Office: Masonic similar offices (e.g., "RWGM", "PM"). Military Status: service status retired (e.g., "USNRET"). : geographic contextual markers part formal titles (e.g., "La", "ZL").

title: Look up nicknames, formal names and a canonical form for first names — nickname_lookup
text: Canonical rule. Spelling root. name moves common spelling variant, repeatedly, common nationally (KATHRYN -> KATHERINE -> CATHERINE; STEVEN -> STEPHEN). Spelling pairs come reviewed lexicon , default, misspelling rows (rare form common name, used rare form fewer 1,000 national records: MARCO misspelling MARK). Nickname step. name whose spelling family mostly carried nickname, least min_nick_rate people name (MARK, name right, resolved MARCUS), resolved formal name. direct formal partners grouped spelling root weighted number people carrying pair; partners nicknames dropped others exist; known gender, partners gender dropped. top group wins least min_share weight. Otherwise name "ambiguous" keeps spelling root (KATHY: KATHLEEN vs KATHERINE; AL: ALAN vs ALBERT; PAT gender). Chains followed: one nickname step , KATHLEEN CATHERINE merged KATE. Gender comes gendered salutation (MR, MRS, MS, MISS), otherwise gender gender_confidence >= min_confidence.

what: Name parsing: title vs. given-name / surname collisions
title: peopleparser (development version)
text: Given names miscategorized credentials prx prefix list (EARL, ZOLA) removed, records like EARL FAHNESTOCK longer lose first name salutation stripping. parse_name() gained general recovery step: stripping salutation leaves first name removed token known census name, restored — role decided original position. leading token given name (EARL FAHNESTOCK -> first EARL); trailing token surname remaining token becomes first name (TOM MAJOR -> first TOM, last MAJOR). Gender recomputed resolved first name. Real titles/credentials (MR, DR, REV, …) unaffected: census names, never restored first names. Added regression tests covering cases.
